speaker: Dana (AE)
text: Thanks for making the time, Marcus. Before we get into the demo, I'd love to just hear how things are running on your side today.

speaker: Marcus (VP Ops, Ridgeline Freight)
text: Sure. So we move about eleven thousand shipments a month across forty carriers, and honestly the invoicing side of that is where we're bleeding.

speaker: Marcus (VP Ops, Ridgeline Freight)
text: Every carrier sends invoices in a different format. Some are EDI, some are PDFs, two of them still fax. My team manually reconciles those against the rate agreements.

speaker: Dana (AE)
text: How many people are on that reconciliation today?

speaker: Marcus (VP Ops, Ridgeline Freight)
text: Four full-time. And they still only spot-check maybe thirty percent of invoices. We know we're overpaying, we just can't prove which ones.

speaker: Priya (Ops Manager)
text: The big one is accessorial charges. Detention, layover, fuel surcharges. Carriers add them and nobody catches it because checking one invoice takes twenty minutes.

speaker: Dana (AE)
text: So if I'm hearing it right, the core need is automated freight invoice auditing that flags variance against contracted rates.

speaker: Marcus (VP Ops, Ridgeline Freight)
text: Exactly. Ingest any invoice format, compare it to the rate agreement, and tell me what's wrong before we pay it.

speaker: Priya (Ops Manager)
text: And it can't just be a report. My team needs a queue — here are today's twelve disputed invoices, here's the evidence, click to file the dispute with the carrier.

speaker: Dana (AE)
text: An exception workflow rather than a dashboard you have to go looking at.

speaker: Priya (Ops Manager)
text: Right. If it's another dashboard nobody opens it. It has to come to us.

speaker: Marcus (VP Ops, Ridgeline Freight)
text: Put a mobile app on it too. I want to approve disputes from my phone when I'm at a terminal.

speaker: Priya (Ops Manager)
text: Honestly Marcus, I'd push back on that. Nobody on my team is doing invoice work on a phone — they're on dual monitors in the office all day. Mobile would be wasted effort.

speaker: Marcus (VP Ops, Ridgeline Freight)
text: Fair. Scratch the mobile app then. Desktop web is fine, just make the approvals fast.

speaker: Dana (AE)
text: Got it — desktop-first, no mobile in v1. What does this need to talk to on your stack?

speaker: Marcus (VP Ops, Ridgeline Freight)
text: Everything settles in SAP. If it doesn't write back to SAP it's a non-starter, that's hard requirement number one.

speaker: Priya (Ops Manager)
text: And our TMS is McLeod. The shipment data lives there — you'd need that to know what the invoice should have been.

speaker: Dana (AE)
text: SAP write-back and a McLeod integration. Anything on the security side?

speaker: Marcus (VP Ops, Ridgeline Freight)
text: We're mid-market but two of our shippers are pharma, so SOC 2 Type II is table stakes. Procurement won't sign without it.

speaker: Priya (Ops Manager)
text: One more thing — audit trail. If we dispute a charge and the carrier escalates, I need to show exactly what the system saw and when.

speaker: Dana (AE)
text: Immutable audit log on every decision. Noted. How are you thinking about ROI on this?

speaker: Marcus (VP Ops, Ridgeline Freight)
text: Industry says three to five percent of freight spend is overbilled. We spend sixty million a year. Even catching half of that pays for a lot of software.

speaker: Priya (Ops Manager)
text: But I'd want a pilot first. Two carriers, ninety days, show me you actually catch things we missed.

speaker: Dana (AE)
text: A ninety-day pilot scoped to two carriers with a measurable recovery number at the end.

speaker: Marcus (VP Ops, Ridgeline Freight)
text: That's the shape of it. What's pricing look like — is it per seat or percentage of recovery?

speaker: Dana (AE)
text: That's still open on our side, I'll bring options. Anything else that would make or break this?

speaker: Priya (Ops Manager)
text: It has to handle the fax ones. I know that's absurd in this decade, but two carriers aren't changing and they're eight percent of our volume.

speaker: Marcus (VP Ops, Ridgeline Freight)
text: And speed. If an invoice takes a day to process we've already missed the payment window on some of these terms.

speaker: Dana (AE)
text: Same-day processing, all formats including scanned and faxed documents. This is really helpful — let me put this in front of our product team.
